article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: warnings of the epidemic's continuation and challenges to its transmission worldwide.
article.articleSummary:
- Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues, with WHO reporting over 3,500 deaths and about 7,400 infections. The epidemic is not centralized; eastern DRC hosts multiple small outbreaks across several provinces, complicating surveillance and control as the geographic extent expands. Some areas show stabilization in new cases, but transmission remains deadly and uneven, demanding sustained field response and access to affected communities. Ebola spreads primarily through contact with blood or body fluids of an infected person or the deceased, not through respiratory routes, underscoring the importance of isolating cases and tracing contacts to interrupt chains of transmission. As of the outbreak’s declaration on May 15, cases have surged to 7,541 with 3,639 deaths across six northern and eastern provinces, despite weak health infrastructure and security instability. Because Bundibugyo has no approved vaccine or treatment, authorities launched mass vaccination of frontline workers in Ituri province on September 19 using Ervebo, which previously showed high protection against other Ebola strains. WHO approved 70,000 doses for DRC: about 50,000 for frontline healthcare workers and at-risk staff; 20,000 for a large clinical study on protection against Bundibugyo. - Bunia, Democratic Republic of the Congo — A vaccination campaign began for 50,000 frontline health workers using Merck’s Ervebo Ebola vaccine, targeting Ituri’s Bunia and Mongbwalu and extending into Nord Kivu. Ervebo was developed for the Zaire strain, but the current outbreak is Bundibugyo, for which no licensed vaccine or therapy exists; efficacy remains uncertain. The WHO authorized 70,000 doses for compassionate use in August, with 20,000 vaccinees monitored for a year. Since May, the outbreak has caused at least 3,639 deaths and about 7,541 infections, with 1,823 recoveries. Some 3,000 people have already been immunized; Bunia’s campaign doubles as field data on Ervebo’s protection against Bundibugyo. Nord Kivu cases exceed 200 weekly, while Ituri and South Kivu show variable trends.
- As of 20 September 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), caused by the Bundibugyo strain, reports 7,541 cases and 3,639 deaths (case fatality rate 48.3%). A frontline vaccination trial began on 19 September 2026, targeting about 20,000 healthcare workers in Ituri and North Kivu provinces to assess the Ervebo vaccine—originally developed for the Zaire strain—for protection against Bundibugyo over up to one year. There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for this outbreak. The initiative is supported by the WHO and MSF. The article notes ongoing transmission with no mention of imported/exported cases.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue fever cases surge in HCM City
article.articleSummary: As of 19 September 2026, dengue fever cases surge in Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC), with 32,626 infections since the start of 2026 and 1,544 new cases in the past week. From Aug 3 to Sep 6, over 1,000 new weekly cases were reported. Dengue circulates year-round, peak activity typically around October, driven by Aedes mosquitoes that breed in clean, stagnant water in household items and outdoor containers. Environmental management and mosquito-control measures are being intensified; vaccination is cited as providing active, long-lasting immunity. Hospitalizations rose through June (>600), July (~1,300), August (>1,500), and early September (~900). Severe dengue is increasing; ICU notes about seven to nine severe cases per week, with some weeks seven or eight. Local responses include rapid vector control: Bà Rịa Ward (28 cases, eight outbreaks) after Long Tâm quarter outbreaks; Hồ Tràm Commune (100 cases, 49 outbreaks) in eight months; Đông Hòa Ward (>525 cases, up 303) with targeted sanitation and larval elimination.

article.articleHeadline: Rabies is dangerous but preventable.
article.articleSummary: Rabies in Vietnam is deadly but preventable with prompt post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). Rabies remains nearly 100% fatal after symptoms, yet early intervention saves lives. Before 2024 about 500,000 people were treated annually; in 2025 this rose to ~1.1 million. In the first seven months of 2026, more than 500,000 dog-bite cases were reported. The National Institute of Infectious and Tropical Diseases notes 30–50 rabies patients treated yearly. WHO urges immediate risk assessment and PEP after bites or scratches from dogs or cats—do not wait for animal testing. Post-bite care requires washing the wound for at least 15 minutes, then vaccination and possibly rabies immunoglobulin or monoclonal antibodies. If animals can be observed for 10 days, it aids risk assessment, but care should not be delayed. Pet vaccination rose to >56% in 2024–2025 but remains below the 70% herd-immunity target. As of Sep 12, 2026, 54 deaths across 21 provinces (8 since early September). A Hanoi workshop on humane euthanasia of dogs and cats was held Sep 18 as part of a 14-ward pilot project.

article.articleHeadline: Warning Signs You Should Not Ignore During the Dengue Season.
article.articleSummary: Dengue cases with diverse presentations were recorded at Hanoi's National Institute of Infectious and Tropical Diseases, including travel-associated infections from Ho Chi Minh City and community transmission, with management complicated in a cancer patient on chemotherapy. A 49-year-old Hanoi woman developed 39°C fever, headache, and myalgia after a trip to TP.HCM; platelet count fell to 45 x10^9/L. A 37-year-old Hanoi woman had fever and headache, self-medicated, then developed high fever and gum bleeding; dengue diagnosed on day 2. A Hanoi woman cared for a daughter near an area with three prior dengue cases. A cancer patient receiving rectal cancer chemotherapy presented with 39–40°C fever, sore throat, productive cough, and flushed skin; early admission led to fever resolution after 7 days and rising platelets, though recovery remained slower. Experts warn against self-treatment and NSAIDs before dengue exclusion, emphasize bleeding warning signs, urge medical assessment, and advocate mosquito-control and vaccination where appropriate.

article.articleHeadline: Warning: Complications of Influenza A
article.articleSummary: In Hanoi, a 4-year-old girl developed acute necrotizing encephalopathy (ANE) associated with Influenza A after fever and respiratory symptoms. She had continuous seizures and coma within 2 days; a throat swab tested positive for Influenza A. She received high-dose immunosuppressive therapy, renal replacement therapy, and intensive neurocritical care at National Children's Hospital, but brain injury progressed and she died two days after admission. ANE is a rare post-viral brain disease, often following Influenza A, caused by an excessive inflammatory response with cytokine release that disrupts the blood-brain barrier, leading to edema, necrosis, coagulopathy and multi-organ involvement. It typically affects children 2-5 years old. No unified treatment protocol exists; early immunosuppression within 24 hours of neurological symptoms may help some cases. Influenza in children is usually mild but can cause pneumonia, myocarditis, encephalitis, respiratory failure or multi-organ injury. Parents should seek urgent care for high fever with seizures or breathing problems; vaccination is advised.

article.articleSummary: Dengue outbreak in Bihar’s capital Patna has intensified, with 270 laboratory-confirmed dengue cases reported in the first 18 days of September. August-end tally was 167, rising to 270 by mid-September, with about 10–15 new patients identified daily. Earlier months saw 44 cases (Jan–Jun) and 26 in July; August registered 97 new cases. Bankipur, Patliputra, and Kankarbagh—the densely populated core areas—record the highest incidence, with Postal Park, Yogipur, and Jakkanpur also reporting cases. Major drivers include dense population, post-monsoon waterlogging, drainage problems, and small water sources around homes. Diagnoses are being made across government facilities and private hospitals; Civil Surgeon Dr. Yogendra Prasad Mandal notes a large share of cases are detected in private clinics and pathology labs. In response, the Nagar Nigam is conducting fogging and anti-larval campaigns, with larvicidal spraying to curb breeding. No information on imported/exported cases is provided.

article.articleHeadline: In Thrissur, mumps is spreading; DMO issues advisory | Stay Safe From Mumps Virus.
article.articleSummary: Thrissur district, Kerala, India, reports an ongoing mumps outbreak as of 19 September 2026. The viral illness spreads mainly through airborne droplets and close contact. The hallmark symptom is swelling under the ear due to parotid gland involvement, which may affect one or both sides. Early symptoms include low-grade fever, headache, pain while opening the mouth or chewing, drooling, loss of appetite, and fatigue. The contagious period extends from two days before parotitis to four to six days after onset. Although children aged 5–15 years are most affected, adults can also be ill and may experience more severe disease. Complications can involve the brain, testes, pancreas, and possibly other organs. Precautionary measures: alert teachers and health workers, keep infected children at home, disinfect items used by patients, wear masks, maintain social distancing, and wash hands with soap.

article.articleHeadline: Contagious Viral Fever: On Which Day Should a Blood Test Be Taken? - Dr. Advice.
article.articleSummary: Viral fever cases are rising in Tirunelveli and surrounding districts of Tamil Nadu as seasonal changes intensify. Hundreds are affected; government and private hospitals are treating fever patients. Tirunelveli Government Medical College has established a 50-bed ward for fever cases. Dr. Nagarthinam, an MD in General Medicine, notes post-COVID fever awareness has increased among the public. Monsoon-related viral fever typically lasts 5–7 days. There is a possibility of waterborne yellow fever-like illness spreading. People should not panic; follow a doctor's advice and avoid self-medication with antibiotics on day one. Measures to prevent mosquito breeding around homes should be implemented. If fever does not subside after five days, a blood test should be done to check for other infections. Fever may include headache; in the first three days, temperature may exceed 100°F, and body aches can persist for up to a week after fever abates.

article.articleHeadline: Doc Talk | Cough Mimicking TB Or Pneumonia? Know When A Fungal Infection Could Be The Clue
article.articleSummary: As of 19 September 2026, a persistent cough in India lasting weeks after antibiotics may signal a fungal lung infection, often misdiagnosed as bacterial pneumonia or smear-negative TB because symptoms overlap. Overuse of antibiotics can promote resistance. Common culprits are Aspergillus (aspergillosis), Mucorales (mucormycosis, 'black fungus'), and Candida (candidiasis). Risk increases with pre-existing lung disease, diabetes, weakened immunity, or prior TB; TB scars can harbor fungi. Diagnosis uses high-resolution CT to detect cavities, nodules, or fungal balls, plus sputum culture and bronchoscopy; blood tests include Galactomannan (Aspergillus) and Beta-D-Glucan; chronic aspergillosis may use Aspergillus antibodies. Treatments are antifungals, not antibiotics, started under supervision. Invasive mucormycosis requires urgent care; Candida pneumonia is uncommon except in ICU/ventilated patients. Seek pulmonology input for persistent symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: Despite zoonotic disease threat, Keralam's veterinary public health wing yet to take shape
article.articleSummary: Kerala remains without a dedicated veterinary public health wing despite a 2014 Potty committee recommendation to establish a unit with a food safety section and animal management and welfare divisions to tackle zoonotic diseases. Since 2018 Nipah outbreaks, fruit bats have been confirmed carriers with case-fatality rates up to 89–91% in severe cases, requiring rapid animal-side surveillance, sampling, and cross-agency coordination for containment. Recurring Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza outbreaks hit Kuttanad and the backwater belt (Alappuzha, Kottayam, Pathanamthitta), triggering culling of over 800,000 birds (2014–2016), about 250,000 more (2021–2022), with further incidents in 2024 and December 2025. Other emerging diseases include African/classical swine fever, Anthrax, and Kyasanur Forest Disease. Stray dogs and rabies pose rising risks: bites rose from 1.35 lakh in 2017 to 3.69 lakh in 2025, rabies deaths from 8 to 33, and a 2019 stray dog population of 2.89 lakh. Officials argue a dedicated wing would enable timely ABC vaccination, extension education, sampling, ring vaccination, culling, and better health department coordination.

article.articleHeadline: Why is dengue fever spreading even in the absence of rain? - Experts reveal shocking information.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever is spreading in many places even when rainfall is absent. Health experts explain that dry periods see households storing drinking water in jars, vessels, tanks, and plastic containers, and if these are left uncovered, Aedes mosquitoes can lay eggs on inner walls just above the water line. Eggs can survive dry conditions for months and hatch into larvae when water returns. Breeding sites include water collected in flower pots, old tires, discarded plastics, coconut husks, and construction materials. Therefore, the belief that dengue arises only during rains is misleading, prompting the need for year-round prevention. To reduce transmission, keep water storage containers tightly closed, cover jars and vessels, and scrub them thoroughly when emptied. Public health authorities urge sustained mosquito-control efforts across affected regions.

article.articleHeadline: STIs Are Not Always Symptomatic; Be Wary of the Risk to Fertility from Chlamydia and Gonorrhea.
article.articleSummary: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) can be asymptomatic yet threaten fertility, particularly with chlamydia and gonorrhea. The bacteria Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae often cause no obvious symptoms, allowing infections to spread. If untreated, they can ascend from the vagina to the uterus and fallopian tubes, triggering pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). PID can scar reproductive tracts, increasing risks of infertility and ectopic pregnancy. In women, chlamydia and gonorrhea may present with symptoms such as abnormal genital discharge or burning during urination; gonorrhea can cause purulent discharge and pain with urination or bowel movements, though symptoms may be absent. Both infections are treatable with antibiotics under medical supervision, highlighting the need for early diagnosis and care to protect fertility.

article.articleHeadline: Be wary as Influenza A surges, UGM nutrition expert reveals that the key to immune system strength is not just from medicine.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A cases are rising across age groups in Indonesia, prompting focus beyond medicines to daily nutrition. Dr. Toto Sudargo, a nutrition expert from UNIMUS and UGM, says immunity is built indirectly through a balanced intake of carbohydrates, protein, fats, vitamins, and vegetables. Indonesian eating habits skew toward quick, carb- and fat-heavy meals, with low vegetable consumption, undermining immune defenses rich in vitamin C and antioxidants. For influenza season, emphasis should be on real, balanced food rather than supplements. Key nutrients include protein for immune cell formation, vitamin C and antioxidants from vegetables and fruit, and fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K that require fat for absorption. Pro-vitamin A sources such as cassava leaves and Melinjo leaves can be prepared in dishes like sayur lodeh with coconut milk to aid absorption.

triage.headline_ja: 警戒せよ、インフルエンザAが急増中 UGMの栄養専門家が免疫力強化の鍵は薬だけではないと明かす
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザAの増加に関する一般的な栄養アドバイス記事であり、公衆衛生上の重大な懸念や異常性、国際的拡大リスクを示す情報がない。
triage.notes: 記事は栄養専門家による免疫力強化のための食事アドバイスが主題で、季節性インフルエンザ増加自体の詳細な疫学情報（症例数、重症度、地域分布等）は記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: After Ebola got out of control, laboratory scientists warn of a major epidemic outbreak in Africa.
article.articleSummary: West African laboratory scientists meeting in Lomé urged governments to strengthen disease surveillance and diagnostic capacity to avert a major outbreak, citing growing health-system vulnerabilities and reliance on vaccines from Western countries. They referenced lessons from Ebola and COVID-19 outbreaks over the past decade. From 2014–2016, the Ebola epidemic killed at least 11,000 people in West Africa, mainly in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Kossi Capo, president of the Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists in Togo, co-chaired the conference, stressing proactive outbreak readiness. In Congo, Bundibugyo ebolavirus has caused more than 3,600 deaths among about 7,500 cases since mid-May, marking the fastest Ebola spread in history. Separately, hantavirus was detected aboard a cruise ship off Cape Verde in May. The African CDC notes official fatality counts may undercount by up to threefold. Sierra Leone’s Arthur Bodouri Kalvin Garber calls for investing in human resources alongside infrastructure.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の制御不能化を受け、検査科学者らがアフリカでの大規模な疫病発生に警鐘
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で進行中とされるエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）が『史上最速の拡大』とされ、致死率も極めて高い（約7,500症例中3,600死亡）と報じられており、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが疑われるため、フルリスク評価への移行が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はローメで開催された西アフリカの検査科学者会議の報告が主体だが、その中でコンゴ民主共和国におけるブンディブギョ株エボラ出血熱の急速拡大（約7,500症例、3,600死亡、5月中旬以降）という重大情報が含まれる。この症例数・致死率は過去のエボラ流行と比較して極めて高く、数値の正確性について公式情報源（WHO/Africa CDC）との照合が必要。カーボベルデでのハンタウイルス検出は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。トーゴ・シエラレオネ等は会議開催地・過去流行地としての言及であり、現在進行中の発生国ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ministry of Public Health Announces Uganda Removed from Ebola Danger Zone
article.articleSummary: As of 19 September 2026, the Ministry of Public Health of Thailand announced that the Republic of Uganda has been removed from the list of Ebola virus disease (EVD) danger zones outside the Kingdom. The proclamation, published in the Royal Gazette (Volume 143, Special Part 228 N), is dated 18 September 2569 BE and takes effect from 19 September 2569 BE. The order designates foreign territories outside Thailand that are Ebola danger zones under the Ebola virus disease act. Consequently, only the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains an Ebola danger zone under the Infectious Diseases Act B.E. 2558, within a single territory. The article does not report any case or death counts.

triage.headline_ja: タイ保健省、ウガンダをエボラ危険地域から除外と発表
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はタイ保健省による行政上の危険地域指定の更新（ウガンダの除外）を報じるものであり、新規症例や死亡者数などの疫学情報は含まれていない。
triage.notes: 記事はタイの行政公示（ウガンダをエボラ危険地域リストから除外）に関するもので、DRCは引き続き危険地域とされているが、具体的な症例数や死亡者数の報告はない。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: The Ebola epidemic's impact also affects Uganda Family Aid.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo have unsettled Uganda, which has reported cases and was officially declared Ebola-free at the end of July. Measures tied to the outbreak persist: border closures with DRC disrupted trade, pushing up prices for materials used by Ugandan artisans and curbing consumer spending, and higher oil and fuel prices due to the Iran war. The Uganda Family Help (Uganda Familienhilfe), founded about three years ago by Joachim Straub, supports Ugandan youths through a training center that teaches hairdressers, tailors, and motorcycle mechanics. It counts 188 graduates, of whom 102 are employed and 49 have started their own businesses; 18 sponsorships are active, with 35 apprentices planned per year. Annual operating costs run about €13,500; training costs are roughly €35 per month per student. Street-front shop relocation rules issued during the Ebola period remain. Straub plans an October visit to advance further goals.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行の影響、ウガンダの家族支援活動にも波及
triage.triage_reason: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行に伴う経済的影響とウガンダの慈善団体活動を紹介する二次的な内容であり、新規の疫学的情報や公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す記述がない。
triage.notes: ウガンダは7月末にエボラ終息宣言済み。記事は国境封鎖による経済的影響と地元NPOの活動報告が主題であり、新たな感染拡大や公衆衛生上の懸念を示す情報はない。

article.articleHeadline: Kasaï: 77 suspected Mpox cases, including 3 deaths and 16 confirmed cases.
article.articleSummary: Kasaï Province reports 16 mpox (monkeypox) cases confirmed by INRB, with 77 suspected mpox cases and 3 deaths, all among mpox suspects in the Luebo health zone. For yellow fever, 11 suspected cases are recorded across Kitangwa (4), Kalonda Ouest (3), Kanzala (3) and Tshikapa (1), with no deaths. Mpox remains the most concerning disease, totaling 77 suspected cases and 3 deaths, with Luebo alone accounting for 38 suspected mpox cases and 13 confirmed; Mushenge (13), Kanzala (11), Mikope (6), Kalonda Ouest (3), Kamuesha (2), Kitangwa (2), Ndjoko-Punda (1) and Tshikapa (1) follow. Governor Chrispin Mukendi Bukasa urged strengthened epidemiological surveillance, closer collaboration with technical services, and measures to improve case management and reduce mortality from epidemic diseases.

triage.headline_ja: カサイ州：Mpox疑い例77件、うち死亡3件、確定16件
triage.triage_reason: DRCカサイ州でMpox（Clade関連）の疑い例77件、確定16件、死亡3件が報告されており、複数の保健地域に拡大している継続的アウトブレイクであるため、IHR基準を2つ以上満たしフルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: 発生地域にKenyaが含まれているが、記事本文はDRCカサイ州のみに言及しており関連性なし。黄熱病の疑い例（11件、死亡なし）も同地域で報告されているが、記事の主眼はMpoxである。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri: an NGO welcomes the government's support in its Ebola response activities - ACP.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 September 2026, in Ituri, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ebola response is bolstered by government backing acknowledged by NGO Alima during a meeting with the military governor in Bunia. Dr Moumouni Kinda notes that state support enables access to populations and mobility around Bunia to deliver humanitarian aid. Alima reports high-quality, rapid field care since the outbreak began, with more than 300 ICU beds jointly managed with the Ministry of Health and partners to speed patient recovery. Despite a general decline in infections in some areas, new Ebola cases have appeared in other localities, requiring targeted health-zone support. The organization operates in Ituri's Irumu, Djugu, Mahagi, and Aru territories and continues research for new therapies and preventive solutions, alongside sustained collaboration with local communities.

triage.headline_ja: イトゥリ:あるNGOが政府によるエボラ対応活動への支援を歓迎
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州で進行中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクにおいて、一部地域で感染減少が見られる一方、新たな症例が他の地域で発生しており、重症度・拡大リスクの観点からIHR基準を2つ以上満たすため。
triage.notes: 既知のエボラ流行の継続的な対応活動に関する記事だが、新規感染地域の出現が報告されており、状況の変化として継続的モニタリングとフルRRAでの再評価が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri: Two People Discharged After Recovering from the Ebola Treatment Center in Logo - ACP
article.articleSummary: Two women recovered from Ebola were discharged today from the Ebola Treatment Center at Logo General Reference Hospital in Mahagi territory, Ituri province, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. With these discharges, total recoveries at the Logo center reach 15. There are currently no suspected or confirmed Ebola cases. Dr. Thomas Eneko, the hospital’s medical director, urged continued adherence to health authorities’ preventive measures to interrupt transmission and to promptly report any suspected cases for immediate intervention. He reiterated the need to follow authorities’ guidance to suppress the transmission chain. The report, dated 19 September 2026, notes ongoing surveillance and isolation efforts in the Logo area as part of outbreak response in Ituri.

triage.headline_ja: イトゥリ州：ロゴのエボラ治療センターで2名が回復し退院 - ACP通信
triage.triage_reason: DRCイトゥリ州で進行中のエボラ対応の経過報告であり、現時点で新規の疑い・確定症例はないとされているが、既知のアウトブレイクが継続中であるため引き続き経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 現時点で疑い例・確定例なしとの報告であり、既存アウトブレイクの改善を示す内容。新規シグナルというより継続中のエボラ対応の状況モニタリングとして扱うのが適切。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: the CUBE, an innovative device to combat the epidemic.
article.articleSummary: Ebola persists in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with ALIMA deploying the CUBE — Chambre d'Urgence Biosécurisée pour Épidémies (Biosafe Emergency Chamber for Epidemics) — at Rwampara in Ituri Province to protect health workers while preserving patient-family contact. The autonomous, modular, transportable unit features transparent walls and built-in gloves, enabling clinicians to treat Ebola patients from outside the chamber while continuously monitoring vitals; some treatments can be administered remotely, reducing staff exposure. Installation takes under 90 minutes and deployment can reach outbreak areas, potentially cutting costs by up to 75% versus traditional treatment centers. Beyond protection, CUBE mitigates isolation by allowing families to see and communicate with relatives. The response is supported by OCHA funding mechanisms. Since 2018, CUBEs have treated over 500 patients with hemorrhagic fevers in DRC, Guinea, and Nigeria.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：流行に対抗する革新的装置「CUBE」
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱が依然として持続しており、重症度が高く人道支援（OCHA資金）の必要性が示されているため、フルリスク評価への移行が妥当と判断される。
triage.notes: 記事はALIMAが開発した治療用装置CUBEの紹介が主眼だが、DRCでのエボラ流行継続と国際支援（OCHA資金）への言及があるため注視が必要。ギニア・ナイジェリアは対象国リスト外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Deadly Ebola outbreak in Congo: 'It is an inhumane disease'
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is the deadliest in the country to date, with official tallies over 7,000 infections and around 3,300 deaths, though sources cite higher figures (over 7,400 infections and about 3,600 deaths). The outbreak continues to spread, nearing the scale of West Africa’s 2014 crisis in growth, according to MSF’s emergency medical manager. Health workers in protective gear treat patients, while community fear and fatalities widen the distance between staff and residents. Ongoing conflict, rebel activity, weak governance, and fragile health infrastructure in Congo hinder response and likely drive transmission. Endemic diseases like malaria and measles persist, adding to public concern. Officials acknowledge that registered infections underestimate true cases, highlighting surveillance gaps during this intensified outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでの致死的なエボラ流行：『それは非人道的な病気だ』
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最悪規模のエボラ流行が拡大中で、感染者7,000人超・死者3,300人超と深刻な公衆衛生上の影響があり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクも懸念されるため。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）でのエボラ流行を主題としており、アンゴラは発生地域として付与されているが本文中で言及されていないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: South Kivu: 20 cholera deaths among more than 1,100 cases in two weeks.
article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreak in South Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, with 20 deaths and over 1,100 cases across epidemiological weeks 36–37 of 2026. Week 36 recorded 482 cases and 7 deaths; week 37 had 651 cases and 13 deaths. Most affected health zones are Bukavu, Kabare, Walungu, and Uvira; within Bukavu, the Ibanda health zone reported 167 cases in week 37. Uvira health zone is second in burden, followed by Shabunda. Since January 2026, the province has 11,854 confirmed cholera cases and 160 deaths, CFR 1.4%. Data provided by Justin Bengheya, Public Health Specialist and Chief of the Health Information and Disease Surveillance Office, Provincial Health Division. Published on September 19, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: 南キブ州：2週間で1,100件以上のコレラ症例中20人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: 南キブ州で急速に拡大するコレラ流行が確認され、2週間で1,100人以上、年初来では約1.2万人・160人死亡と大規模かつ継続的な公衆衛生上の脅威であるため。
triage.notes: DRC南キブ州は既知のコレラ流行地域であり周期的発生は珍しくないが、症例数・死亡数の規模から継続監視とフルリスク評価が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: News | Ebola in Butembo: schools struggle to implement hygiene measures | mediacongo.net.
article.articleSummary: In Butembo, North Kivu’s Nord-Kivu 2 education province faces severe hygiene gaps as schools struggle to implement Ebola virus disease (EVD) prevention amid an ongoing outbreak and insecurity. Reports show inadequate water, soap, and handwashing facilities: Complexe scolaire Alfajiri has only one handwashing device; Kavale Primary uses a single device; Mwenge Primary lacks sufficient equipment and no thermoflash. Some schools have repurposed operating funds to buy handwashing kits, while others with kits still lack water or soap. In Kebikeba (Beni territory), five handwashing devices and two thermoflash units serve 21 classrooms; Katsya Institute has at least three devices but no thermoflash. These conditions persist despite appeals by students and teachers’ unions to bolster sanitation infrastructure. Across the DRC, WHO (as of 7 Sept 2026) reports 6,757 confirmed EBOV cases and 3,267 deaths in 61 health zones across six provinces, with detection delays fueling transmission. The Education Ministry has a differentiated return plan and mandated handwashing devices, thermoflashs, and, where possible, hydroalcoholic gels.

triage.headline_ja: ブテンボのエボラ出血熱：学校が衛生対策の実施に苦慮
triage.triage_reason: DRCで進行中の大規模エボラ流行（WHO報告で6,757人感染、3,267人死亡）に関連し、学校での衛生対策不備が感染拡大リスクを高めている点でIHR基準・WPRO基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 記事は既知の大規模エボラ流行の一環として学校の衛生インフラ不足を報告。流行自体は既存のシグナルである可能性が高いが、感染拡大リスク要因として重要な情報を含むためPICKUPと判定。

article.articleHeadline: Kwango ta fara bai wa ma'aikatan jinya rigakafin Ebola
article.articleSummary: Kwango ta fara bai wa ma’aikatan jinya rigakafin Ebola a Bunia, Ituri, yankin da barkewar ta yi tasiri sosai. An fi fifita rigakafin Ervebo ga ma’aikatan kiwon lafiya a Bunia da Mongbwalu, cikin Ituri, tare da shirin raba rigakafin a cikin watanni shida zuwa tara a Ituri da arewacin Kivu. Gwamnan soji na Ituri, Manjo Janar Gaby Kasongo Mulumba, ya bayyana cewa babban aikin shine kare rayukan jama’a. Ana sa ran ba wa ma’aikatan jinya 20,000 rigakafi. Bayanan WHO sun nuna sama da mutane 7,500 sun kamu da Ebola, kusan 4,000 sun mutu. Barkewar Ebola a Ituri a wannan lokacin ita ce mafi muni, sau 17 fiye da abin da ya gabata a baya. A ranar 19 ga Satumba, 2026, ana ci gaba da aiwatar da rigakafin a yankin.

triage.headline_ja: クワンゴ州、看護師へのエボラワクチン接種を開始
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イツリ州で過去最大規模（従来の17倍）とされるエボラ流行が継続中で、感染者7,500人超・死者約4,000人と深刻な公衆衛生影響があり、WHO主導のワクチン接種が行われている。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Epidemic: Russia Delivers Tests to Uganda
article.articleSummary: Russia’s Rospotrebnadzor delivered 7,000 diagnostic test kits for the Ebola Bundibugyo virus to Uganda to speed detection of suspected cases, with the supply also intended for the Democratic Republic of Congo as the outbreak expands. The Ugandan Health Ministry organized the shipment, designed for 7,000 tests, and Ugandan and Russian specialists had previously field-tested the assays in Uganda during a May-June Ebola Bundibugyo fever outbreak, reporting high diagnostic accuracy. The handover ceremony was attended by Dr. Charles Olaro, Uganda's Director General of Health Services, who praised the cooperation. In the DRC, the outbreak now spans seven provinces, with 7,475 confirmed cases, 1,798 recoveries, and 3,605 deaths reported as of 16 September 2026. The tests are intended to accelerate laboratory confirmation of suspected Ebola Bundibugyo virus infections in both countries.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行:ロシアがウガンダに検査キットを提供
triage.triage_reason: DRCで7,475症例・3,605死亡、7州に拡大する大規模エボラ(ブンディブギョ株)流行であり、国際的な検査支援も行われているためIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。

article.articleHeadline: Climate change reshapes the malaria hotspot map in Africa.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026, climate change reshapes malaria transmission across sub-Saharan Africa. A century-spanning analysis of blood samples from 1901–2014 uses a computer model linking pediatric malaria prevalence to temperature and rainfall, comparing with a no-climate-change scenario. It finds a net 0.5% increase in malaria transmission across SSA due to warming, with larger rises in East and Southern Africa and declines in parts of West Africa (1–2%). In the Ethiopian highlands, transmission rose by about 8 additional cases per 1,000 children. Historically hot spots in Nigeria and the Democratic Republic of Congo are shifting toward eastern and southern Africa. Projections under a mid-range warming of 2.7°C over about 85 years suggest SSA malaria transmission could fall by around 2%. The authors urge expanded vector control—treated nets, insecticides—and preventive antimalarial drugs.

triage.headline_ja: 気候変動がアフリカのマラリア流行地図を変える
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は1901〜2014年の長期データに基づく気候変動とマラリア伝播の学術的研究報告であり、特定の急性アウトブレイクや異常事態を報じるものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はマラリア伝播パターンの気候変動による長期的変化を分析した研究に基づくもので、DRCは歴史的ホットスポットとして言及されているが現在進行中のアウトブレイクではない。Angola、Ethiopia、Mozambique、Nigeriaは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: The Congo has begun vaccinating health workers against Ebola in the city of Bunia, the outbreak so far the fastest-spreading Ebola epidemic in history.
article.articleSummary: Ebola vaccination campaign begins in Bunia, Congo, with health workers inoculated as the outbreak is described as the fastest-spreading Ebola epidemic in history. In Mali, jihadist attack on a military base left at least 100 Malian soldiers dead and five members of the Africa Corps (Wagner group). In Ceuta, Spain, authorities relocated about 1,700 migrants from two beaches to a port camp due to dire hygienic conditions; more than 2,000 remain on beaches. In Yemen, fighting along the coast has displaced at least 112,000 people in two weeks, with around 3,000 fleeing by sea to Djibouti per UNHCR. In Nigeria, at least 37 detainees died in a hospital after arrest on suspicion of illegal mining; authorities cite a disease outbreak, while a survivor cites possible suffocation from overcrowding. In South Africa near Johannesburg, investigators report a ninth corpse since July; police are examining the possibility of a serial killer.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴがブニアでエボラワクチン接種を開始、史上最速の拡大を見せる流行
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国ブニアで史上最速拡大とされるエボラ流行に対しワクチン接種開始という重大な公衆衛生イベントであり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。

article.articleHeadline: Xiao Tongwen's mother hospitalized with influenza complicated by pneumonia; father worries she won't be able to speak at all.
article.articleSummary: On Sept 18, 2026, the article reports that elderly mother of TV host Xiao Tongwen was hospitalized with influenza A complicated by pneumonia. She woke around 4:00 a.m. unable to move, and an ambulance transported her to hospital, where she was admitted to an isolation ward after evaluation. Staff noted she initially had difficulty speaking but remained conscious. Her condition improved after receiving a nearly 3,000 yuan self-paid influenza vaccine shot, and by the third day of hospitalization her mental status had rapidly progressed with expectation of discharge soon. The father tested negative for influenza and has a mild cold. Xiao Tongwen urges seniors to receive influenza and pneumococcal vaccines, stressing that vaccination lowers the risk of severe disease even if infection occurs.

triage.headline_ja: 蕭彤雯氏の母、インフルエンザ合併肺炎で入院；父は「もう話せなくなるのでは」と心配
triage.triage_reason: 個人（著名人の家族）の単発症例報告であり、公衆衛生上の異常事態や拡大リスクを示す情報がないため見送りとする。
triage.notes: 台湾の著名人家族の個人的な健康事例に関する報道であり、季節性インフルエンザの流行状況を示すものではない。地域も台湾であり対象国リストに含まれない。

article.articleHeadline: This course will be crucial once the new semester begins! For this disease, 98.5% of infections are sexually transmitted. Pre-exposure protection and post-exposure testing are indispensable.
article.articleSummary: HIV/AIDS in China: 98.5% of infections are sexually transmitted, per the 2025 national HIV/AIDS transmission report. Heterosexual transmissions account for 63,960 cases (72.8%), homosexual transmissions 22,564 cases (25.7%), with a male-to-female ratio of 3.5:1. Acute and asymptomatic HIV infections have no distinguishing signs and cannot be identified by appearance; testing is essential. The article urges lifelong HIV/AIDS awareness, protective practices before sex, and proactive testing and timely interventions. Pre-exposure protection (PrEP) and post-exposure testing are indispensable. After high-risk exposure, initiate prophylaxis as soon as possible within 24 hours and no later than 72 hours, continuing for 28 days. Set against the new university semester in China, the piece emphasizes personal health responsibility and education to prevent transmission.

article.articleHeadline: A chef in Chongqing allegedly drew blood in the restaurant to test for HIV.
article.articleSummary: Chongqing, China—In Liangjiang New Area, a restaurant chef was accused online of drawing blood in the shop to test for HIV using a rapid test kit; a post dated Sept 19 shows the chef handling a test strip with packaging branded Jissbon. The post prompted calls for clarification; the restaurant owner told reporters the claim is false and investigators are involved; he said the chef was unwell and only attempting to check for hepatitis B, not HIV. The Liangjiang New District Market Supervision and Administration Bureau said staff were not on duty yet and would follow up the next day. Jissbon's official store confirmed the product can be used to test for HIV and includes hepatitis B surface antigen among its tests. No laboratory-confirmed cases or tests have been reported; the situation remains under investigation.

article.articleHeadline: Tourist at Huangshan bitten by a troop of monkeys, given eight doses of rabies vaccine; doctor: seeing blood constitutes Category III exposure.
article.articleSummary: On Sept 18 at Huangshan, a female tourist was reportedly surrounded by monkeys and received eight doses of rabies vaccine plus immunoglobulin; the incident drew public attention to post-exposure management. Zhengzhou People’s Hospital Emergency Department chief Dr. Qi Wentao notes rabies risk depends on animal species: cats and dogs are most common, but other mammals (including big cats, raccoons, weasels, skunks) and larger rodents can transmit; bats are high-risk and any bat exposure is treated as Level 3. Rabies exposure is categorized into three levels: Level 1—wash with water only; Level 2—vaccine plus local wound cleaning (rinsing with running water for at least 15 minutes, then iodine); Level 3—vaccine plus rabies immunoglobulin, dosed roughly 20 IU per 10 kg body weight. Facial exposure or exposure via licking/kissing mucous membranes is Level 3, as is any bleeding exposure. Rabies has a 100% fatality rate once infected. A second tourist also reported monkey bites the same day.

article.articleHeadline: Yingtan CDC reminds: Flu prevention should be started as early as possible.
article.articleSummary: Yingtan CDC urges early influenza prevention as schools reopen. In Hangzhou, a class of 40 saw 10 with fever and nearly half diagnosed with flu, prompting a four-day suspension. Flu visits rise in the first days of school. The season dominated by influenza A(H3N2); about 90% of outbreaks occur in schools and nurseries, with young students most affected. Crowded classrooms and limited ventilation facilitate spread, while immunity wanes as the virus evolves. Schools should enforce strict entry screening, daily fever/cough checks, isolate cases, and require 48 hours fever-free before return; ensure ventilation and regular disinfection of high-touch surfaces; report clusters promptly. Students should wash hands, cover coughs, avoid sharing items, and get at least 2 hours of daily physical activity. Parents should monitor health, seek prompt care, and vaccinate. Vaccination is advised from Sept–Oct; protection develops in 2–4 weeks, and egg allergy is not a blanket contraindication. Source: Yingtan CDC.

article.articleHeadline: Rising dengue infections: Qdenga vaccine to be available for use next year.

Japan-based Takeda Pharmaceuticals’ QDENGA dengue vaccine will be introduced in India, after a contract signed on Sept 18, 2026 between Takeda and Hyderabad’s Dr. Rettis. The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation approved marketing in July 2026, with use expected by June 2027. Two-dose efficacy against dengue reported at 90.4%. The vaccine is already used in over 40 countries, including the United Kingdom, Brazil, Switzerland, Malaysia, and Thailand, and WHO recommends its deployment in high-burden settings. Globally, more than 24 million doses have been delivered.

article.articleHeadline: Can plant-based milk be left out of the fridge? An Unicamp study warns of the risk of bacteria.
article.articleSummary: Unicamp researchers tested five plant-based milks—oat, almond, cocoa with cashew, and pea beverages—and found growth of Bacillus cereus, Escherichia coli, and Salmonella typhimurium at 25°C (ambient). At 37°C, E. coli and S. typhimurium grew more rapidly; B. cereus growth was less temperature-dependent but higher in drinks with more protein, fiber, and energy. The study, from the Food Engineering Faculty at Universidade Estadual de Campinas, published in June in the Journal of Food Science, shows microbial proliferation can occur without refrigeration and is shaped by formulation. Ingredients like cocoa, sugars, water activity, pH, and mineral content (notably sodium and calcium) influence outcomes, while cocoa polyphenols may modulate growth. Authors advocate stable formulations, strict storage controls, raw-material quality, and production hygiene; where needed, lowering pH or reformulating to reduce pathogen risk, plus temperature control after manufacture.

article.articleHeadline: With 47 cases, the health department intensifies active tuberculosis case finding.
article.articleSummary: Barretos Epidemiological Surveillance in Barretos, Brazil, intensified active tuberculosis case finding from Sept 16 to Sept 30, 2026. The campaign targets individuals with cough lasting two weeks or more who should visit a Basic Health Unit for testing; specimens are sent to Ribeirão Preto for analysis. Despite routine year-round activities, the effort doubles twice annually. So far in 2026 Barretos has 47 TB cases, up from 40 in the same period in 2025. Health agents conduct home visits and outreach in clinic waiting rooms; positive cases are referred to the Infectious Diseases Outpatient Clinic for treatment and specialized follow-up. The surveillance program also screens family members and close contacts, given tuberculosis transmission commonly occurs in enclosed spaces.

article.articleHeadline: Ceará records 243 cases and 21 deaths from meningitis in 2026; see symptoms and how to prevent.
article.articleSummary: Ceará, Brazil: 243 confirmed meningitis cases in 2026 through Sept 7, with 22 deaths after a 12-year-old girl in Quixeramobim died on Sept 14; numbers are preliminary and may be revised as investigations consolidate (Sesa/Sinan). The outbreak context notes most meningitis is viral, but bacterial forms cause greater concern; the Quixeramobim fatality was laboratory-confirmed as pneumococcal meningitis (Streptococcus pneumoniae). Common symptoms include fever, headache, nausea, vomiting, and neck pain. Vaccination is key prevention, with meningococcal vaccines C and ACWY, pneumococcal, and pentavalent vaccines protecting against meningitis-causing agents. In the public system, meningococcal C is given at 3 and 5 months with a 12-month booster; ACWY is advised for adolescents 11–14. For suspected cases, seek medical care promptly; close contacts are assessed by health teams to determine preventive measures.

article.articleHeadline: The strongest El Niño could worsen diseases and strain health systems
article.articleSummary: OPAS releases the first regional report on a 'Super El Niño,' with NOAA estimating a very intense event and likelihood >90%. As of 2026-09-19, more than 5.2 million people in the Americas are exposed to health risks or food insecurity. Eight countries face drought or water scarcity; six report wildfires affecting health; five endure heavy rains or floods. The report warns El Niño can intensify mosquito- and water-borne diseases, heat exposure, air-quality decline, and disruptions to health services. Previous El Niños coincided with Zika and chikungunya (2015–2016) and record dengue transmission (2023–2024). Brazil: 630 cities report PM2.5 above WHO guidelines, though no health problems confirmed yet; Inmet projects northern/Northeastern droughts and southern rains. Across the region: Central America drought; Guatemala ~3 million hungry; Honduras ~2 million. Colombia faces dengue surge, malaria, yellow fever; Peru—floods/landslides—at least 70 deaths and >600 health facilities affected. Contingency plans urged.

article.articleHeadline: Samples collected for brucellosis in Santa Isabel, Colón.
article.articleSummary: On 19 September 2026, 100 blood samples were collected for the diagnosis of bovine brucellosis and 20 calves were ear-tagged at the farm of producer Antonio Araúz in the Nombre de Dios corregimiento, Santa Isabel district, Costa Arriba, Colón province. Bovine brucellosis is an infectious disease caused by Brucella abortus, affecting cattle and potentially transmissible to humans. Angel Gómez, head of the MIDA extension in Palenque agency, said the activity aims to reinforce prevention and control of conditions impacting herd health and farm productivity. Veterinarian Health Animal assistant José Luis Vergara carried out the blood sampling as part of epidemiological work. The tagging of 20 calves helps correct identification and individual records to maintain better herd control. Santa Isabel district has high cattle activity, prompting sanitary surveillance across the area.

article.articleHeadline: Nobody knows how it happened, the researcher was astonished: a predatory bird spreading a devastating disease was found in Europe.
article.articleSummary: Alive predatory kissing bug Hospesneotomae protracta was found in Europe for the first time: a single female in a Lisbon hotel in August 2025. The insect, native to the US Southwest and northwestern Mexico, feeds on human blood and can transmit Trypanosoma cruzi, the agent of Chagas disease. The Lisbon specimen tested 100% positive for H. protracta by morphology and DNA sequencing and did not carry T. cruzi, suggesting no transmission in Europe yet. How the bug arrived remains uncertain; luggage or shipping are plausible. The travelers were from the Americas, underscoring imported risk. Chagas disease incubation spans weeks to months; acute symptoms include fever, muscle pain, and swollen glands. About 30–45% develop chronic cardiac disease over 10–20 years, contributing to roughly 10,000 deaths annually, with about 8 million infected and 200,000 new infections per year. The disease is most common in tropical South America; related vectors occur in Brazil.

article.articleHeadline: Peru Reports 67 Dengue Deaths So Far This Year
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever in Peru climbs amid El Niño-driven heat: 67 dengue deaths and 55,943 cases were recorded from January through September this year, a 79% rise from the same period in 2025. The northern coast near Ecuador and Amazonian regions—where temperatures have stayed above 30°C—bear the heaviest burden. For comparison, January–September 2025 saw 31,266 cases and 51 deaths. Health officials attribute the surge to unusually warm temperatures that promote mosquito reproduction, with authorities preparing an epidemiological alert ahead of the rains. The regions most affected are Piura, La Libertad and Lambayeque in the north, plus Ucayali, Loreto and Madre de Dios on the eastern border with Brazil. In 2024 Peru reported over 271,000 dengue cases, underscoring dengue as a tropical-endemic disease with symptoms including high fever, headaches, nausea, vomiting, muscle pain, and risk of hemorrhage.

Emphasis was placed on sanitary surveillance and early case identification as essential for animal health and public health. The session expands access to information on prevention, surveillance and herd-health management among Estrela Dalva producers.

article.articleHeadline: Zero Note: Pruning transforms the square in Bairro Feliz into a dump and a mosquito breeding ground.
article.articleSummary: More than ten days, residents and visitors to Praça Pedro Gorneiro at the entrance of Bairro Feliz, between Avenida Laurício Pedro Rasmussen and L-1/L-10, have endured neglect as pruning debris—large quantities of leaves and dry branches—occupy almost the entire public space with no removal by authorities. The vegetal waste poses direct safety and public health risks, can fuel fires, and, when it rains, retains water, creating an ideal breeding ground for Aedes aegypti, the mosquito vector for dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. The situation hinders mobility and tarnishes the municipal administration’s image. The report, published by zerooudez.com.br on 2026-09-19, underscores ongoing vector-related risk in this area and calls for municipal cleanup to mitigate potential outbreaks.

article.articleHeadline: With a rise in measles cases in the North, specialists advise on how to differentiate it from chickenpox.
article.articleSummary: Measles cases rise in Brazil’s North, with 36 confirmed in 2026 across Amazonas, including imported cases from Peru in Tabatinga, near the border. Roraima, a strategic surveillance state, faces potential reintroduction due to geographic proximity and prior viral circulation, though no large outbreak yet. Measles is highly contagious and airborne; initial symptoms include high fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, and light sensitivity, followed by a rash that starts on the face and spreads bodywide. By contrast, chickenpox (varicella-zoster) features itchy vesicles at different stages, from spots to crusts. Vaccination with the MMR (triple viral) vaccine, available free via SUS, remains the main prevention. Brazil regained measles elimination status in 2024 but lost it in 2019; sustaining high coverage is essential, especially in border regions. Challenges in the North include logistics, misinformation, and access to care; emphasize updated calendars, border vigilance, active vaccination campaigns, and rapid response to suspected cases.

article.articleHeadline: Fever from communicable diseases in Mumbai; 5,984 malaria cases and 2,161 dengue cases reported in three months.
article.articleSummary: Three-month period in Mumbai saw malaria 5,984 cases, dengue 2,161, and leptospirosis 277. From January to September 2026, the city also recorded chikungunya 59, H1N1 488, and gastroenteritis 2,050, alongside the malaria and dengue tallies of 5,984 and 2,161 and leptospirosis 277. Aedes and Anopheles breeding sites were identified at 15,143 locations, with 11,376 of those being Aedes sites. A total of 2,793,193 residents were surveyed, and 32,114 blood samples were sent to laboratories for testing. article.articleHeadline: African swine fever threatens to wipe out several species: not only pigs are at risk.
article.articleSummary: ASF emerged in China in late 2018 and has spread across Asia-Pacific, threatening Asia’s rare wild suids. A Nature Reviews Biodiversity analysis warns the virus could push several island-endemic populations toward extinction within a single generation. The authors propose an eight-point plan to safeguard 12 endemic Asian suid species, with urgent actions including rapid outbreak detection, securing reproductive stocks in captivity, and sustained funding. In the wild, ASF has been confirmed in four species—Sulawesi babirusa (Babyrousa celebensis), Sulawesi wild boar (Sus celebensis), Philippine warty pig (Sus philippensis), and bearded pig (Sus barbatus)—with strong suspicion in Visayan warty pig (Sus cebifrons) and Mindoro warty pig (Sus oliveri). On Sulawesi, both babirusa and boar are affected; the babirusa is evolutionarily distinct, with tusks that grow through the snout. In Borneo, bearded pig declines affect local communities; wild suids contribute to soil modification, seed dispersal, and predator prey. Only five of twelve species are in ex situ programs, leaving time to intervene limited.

triage.notes: ASFは人に感染しないため公衆衛生上の直接的リスクはなく、内容は野生動物（希少イノシシ科）の保全問題が主題。中国は2018年の発生起源として言及されているのみで、現在の主題地域ではないためverified_locationsから除外。

article.articleHeadline: Naga hospital adds beds as dengue cases reach 600
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Naga City, Camarines Sur, has reached about 600 cases as of Sept. 17, 2026, prompting Naga City General Hospital to add beds along hallways after wards reached full capacity to accommodate a potential surge in patients. The city government declared a state of calamity and intensified containment measures, empowering barangays and adopting a calamity-response mindset; officials report a downtrend in cases and daily monitoring of safeguards. Hospital staff remain on alert, with hospital chief Dr. Joseph Sanchez noting ongoing dengue treatment. A mother, Remy Nobleza, said her son, diagnosed with dengue, received prompt medical attention and is recovering. The situation highlights strain on local health facilities amid rising dengue activity, with authorities emphasizing containment and readiness for possible surges.

article.articleHeadline: Davao Region logs 1.6% increase in dengue cases in August
article.articleSummary: Davao Region, Philippines, reports a 1.6% rise in dengue cases over the August two-week period, with 1,339 cases from August 9–22, up from 1,318 in the prior two weeks. Cumulative cases from January through the first week of September total 10,808, though officials say this is still lower than the same period in 2025. The Department of Health warns the public to seek medical care promptly and avoid self-medication. Mild dengue typically presents with high fever, skin rashes, dizziness, and body aches; warning signs of severe dengue include severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding from gums or nose, vomiting blood, blood in stool, and extreme fatigue. Without timely treatment, severe dengue can cause life-threatening bleeding, a sudden drop in blood pressure, and death.

article.articleHeadline: Locally transmitted dengue fever reported in Changhua County! A man in his thirties with no overseas travel history — 'Fever did not improve' diagnosed on his second medical visit.
article.articleSummary: Locally transmitted dengue fever reported in Changhua County, Taiwan: A man in his 30s with no overseas travel history was diagnosed with dengue fever on Sept 17, 2026. He lives in Changhua City; symptoms began in early September with fever and, after no improvement, he sought urgent care and testing confirmed dengue virus type 1. Symptoms include fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia/arthralgia, and rash. He is hospitalized; close contacts have no symptoms. This year Taiwan has 11 local dengue cases, with Kaohsiung City accounting for 10 and Changhua County for 1; total confirmed cases reach 168 by Sept 17, including 157 imported infections, mainly from Vietnam (38), Indonesia (28), and the Philippines (20). Authorities have deployed emergency vector-control, larval-source reduction, and risk assessment around the residence and activities, plus education. Public advised to practice 'round, drain, empty, scrub' and seek care for fever with possible dengue symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: Another West Nile fever case was reported, and meningitis was also registered.
article.articleSummary: During the 36th week (Aug 31–Sep 6, 2026), Hungary reported increases in common infections: 183 Salmonellosis, 130 Campylobacteriosis, 42 rotavirus gastroenteritis, and 50 hepatitis A cases, up from the previous week (Salmonellosis 111; Campylobacteriosis 124; hepatitis A 43). Baranya County recorded six Salmonellosis cases, plus one Campylobacteriosis and one Rotavirus case, and one serous meningitis case; no new Baranya cases of hepatitis A, scarlet fever, varicella, or whooping cough. Dengue virus was detected in a 43-year-old man living in Pest County who had recently stayed in the Philippines during incubation. West Nile fever rose to four cases in 2026, including an 83-year-old man hospitalized in Budapest with neurological symptoms; overall, 75% of the patients are male, mean age 68.3 years. All West Nile cases required hospitalization.

article.articleHeadline: Thailand adds Legionnaires, SFTS, RSV and shingles to disease watch list
article.articleSummary: Thailand added Legionnaires' disease, severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and shingles to its list of notifiable diseases, meaning clinicians must report every case to the Department of Disease Control. The decision was approved at the national communicable disease committee’s fifth meeting of the year, held Sept. 18 at the Department of Disease Control, chaired by Public Health Minister Phatthana Phromphat. The move aims to improve tracking of how far and how quickly each disease spreads. Separately, the committee reviewed a draft national immunisation programme to give vaccine records a formal legal footing and integrate disparate records held by state hospitals, local authorities, and private providers. A subcommittee will coordinate among agencies, and private providers are urged to report vaccine doses to the national system.

article.articleHeadline: WHO advances talks on pathogen access to confront future pandemics lishing
article.articleSummary: On 19 September 2026, WHO member states advanced negotiations on a pathogen access and benefit-sharing (PABS) system intended to speed and equity in pandemic responses. The eighth Intergovernmental Working Group meeting in Geneva focused on the PABS annex of the WHO Pandemic Agreement, adopted by the WHA in 2025, aiming to rapidly share pathogen materials and sequences with pandemic potential while ensuring equitable access to vaccines, therapeutics, and diagnostics developed from their use. Tedros Ghebreyesus said progress brings countries closer to strengthening global preparedness post-COVID-19. The negotiations precede the UN General Assembly High-Level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response in New York (Sept 25), which is expected to urge timely completion of the PABS annex. Leadership changed: Dr Ahmed Al-Mandhari (Oman) elected as vice chairman, alongside Ambassador Vuyile Dlamini (Eswatini) and Dr Viroj Tangcharoensathien (Thailand).

article.articleHeadline: Rumors spoiled the beach mood: Thai authorities revealed the real situation regarding the coronavirus.
article.articleSummary: Rumors of a new coronavirus surge in Thailand are unfounded, per Thailand's National Department of Communicable Diseases. As of Sep 15, 2026, Thailand logged 135,700 COVID-19-like infections, about 0.2% of the population; Phuket and Chonburi saw 0.5% and 0.6%. By mid-September 2025, infections were around 500,000, much higher. There are no quarantines or travel restrictions; resorts, beaches, and attractions operate normally, with few people wearing masks on tourist sites. Medical experts warn that seasonal influenza and diarrheal diseases pose greater risk in the tropics, mitigated by hand hygiene and cautious street-food choices. Russian tour operators report no wave of trip cancellations; travelers face no medical or administrative barriers. The article notes the situation is calmer than a few years ago and advises keeping normal precautions rather than delaying vacations.

article.articleHeadline: Chiang Mai University doctors warn: It's no longer just about dogs and cats. Get to know SFTS, a tick-borne disease that humans can contract, causing high fever and low platelets, and may be life-threatening.
article.articleSummary: On 19 September 2026, Chiang Mai University clinicians warn that Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS), a tick-borne virus, can affect humans. Surveillance data show 6 SFTS cases (2025–2026) with 5 deaths; two fatalities occurred in Phetchabun Province in the north. SFTSV was detected in ticks around the homes of the deceased and in dogs owned by them. Transmission is mainly by infected tick bites; contact with blood or secretions may also spread. Symptoms appear 5–14 days after exposure and include high fever, fatigue, headache, nausea/vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and altered consciousness. Lab findings may show leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, and abnormal liver/kidney function; severe cases may develop acute kidney injury, myocarditis, arrhythmias, meningitis, or encephalitis. Prevention: check pets for ticks and use vet-recommended preventatives; avoid handling ticks bare-handed and avoid blood contact. Outdoors, wear long clothing, use repellents, and check for ticks after exposure. Seek care promptly and inform doctors about tick bites or animal exposure.

triage.triage_reason: タイ国内でSFTS（重症熱性血小板減少症候群）による6例中5例の死亡という高致死率が報告されており、公衆衛生上深刻かつ新興感染症として異常性が高いためフルリスク評価が必要と判断した。
triage.notes: 6例中5例死亡という高い致死率が報告されており、ダニ媒介に加え血液・分泌物接触による感染拡大の可能性も指摘されている。続報でヒト-ヒト感染の実態や地理的拡大の有無を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Government Flags Off Anthrax Vaccination in Muchinga - ZNBC
article.articleSummary: Anthrax vaccination campaign flagged off in Muchinga Province, Zambia, targeting 20,000 domestic animals across Mpika (outbreak epicenter), Shiwang'andu, and Lavushimanda districts. The launch in Mpika aims to contain the Anthrax outbreak with government-led rapid vaccine deployment and resource mobilization. District Commissioner David Siame highlighted the drive as vital to safeguarding lives and the livestock sector, linking it to national goals of expanding the cattle herd to 7 million and achieving US$1 billion in beef exports. Provincial Fisheries and Livestock Coordinator Dr. Nasilele Kalonga stated no domestic animals have been affected so far, and beef, pork, mutton, and goat meat remain safe for consumption. Farmers in the targeted areas are urged to bring animals forward for vaccination to ensure the campaign’s success.

article.articleHeadline: Ghana begins free rabies vaccination for 25,000 pets
article.articleSummary: Ghana launches a free rabies vaccination campaign for 25,000 dogs and cats in identified high-risk areas during September 2026, part of World Rabies Month and the drive to eliminate human deaths from dog-mediated rabies by 2030. The initiative, announced by the Veterinary Services Department and signed by Chief Veterinary Officer Dr Emmanuel Allegye-Cudjoe, offers free vaccination throughout September; a fee applies afterwards. Public education will be expanded via schools, religious institutions, traditional and social media, with materials in Twi, Ga, Ewe and Hausa. Owners are urged to vaccinate annually and to report animal bites or scratches to the nearest health facility and to register the animal at the nearest veterinary centre. Rabies is virtually 100% fatal once symptoms develop but preventable by vaccination. Support from MMDAs, CSOs, religious/traditional authorities, development partners and the private sector is sought for vaccines, logistics and outreach.
